html:
SMTO-BOOT-0008 — Part of SMTO's installation is incomplete

GUID: 75b3d38d-4e98-406a-89eb-9f78af98b0dc
Slug: boot-runtime-incomplete
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The Gateway or SMTO checked its installed parts and found something missing or out of date, or it was started in a way this kind of installation doesn't support. It stopped before starting.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If Tasks are running on this Gateway, let them finish or stop them before repairing it. You'll restart the Gateway after the repair, which would interrupt work in progress.
  2. Run the installer for this computer again: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on a Mac, or src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Use ./install.sh if SMTO itself was updated too. The installer repairs missing or mismatched parts in place without removing the Gateway's pairing or settings.
  3. If you started an installed (packaged) copy of SMTO with --reload, start it again without that option. The --reload option only works when running from source code, and installed copies refuse it.
  4. Once the Gateway starts again, begin a new Task instead of continuing an older one. Existing Tasks keep the list of tools they saw when they started, so only a new Task sees the repaired Gateway.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway or SMTO starts without this error, and a new Task can use the tools you expect.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message, including the Error reference line and any installer log path it mentions, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the Gateway's pairing, settings, browser profiles or Task files to start fresh.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A startup readiness check or installer dependency step failed: gateway_core.runtime_readiness found missing, incompatible or editable Gateway modules, the macOS or Windows installer's pip/update_gateway_runtime step failed, or the packaged entry point rejected its runtime context (missing resources, unsupported compiled metadata, unsupported default expression or --reload).

What this means

  • Runtime readiness or dependency installation fails, or packaged startup rejects invalid runtime-root/interpreter/default/reload/lifecycle assumptions. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Runtime readiness or dependency installation fails, or packaged startup rejects invalid runtime-root/interpreter/default/reload/lifecycle assumptions.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual component and failed readiness/package/startup invariant; this family is not limited to Gateway dependencies.

How to fix it

  • Read the preceding output (readiness remediation, the installer log path, or the ValueError/RuntimeError text), settle active jobs, then rerun the matching installer: src/gateway_agent/install.sh, src/gateway_macos/install.sh, src/gateway_windows/install.ps1, or install.sh when the Server was also updated. Packaged builds must use their own launcher and must not be started with --reload. Afterwards restart the Gateway, refresh its metadata and start a new Task, because existing Tasks keep their captured capability snapshot; granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.
  • Repair the named component's installation or startup configuration using its matching supported entry point; settle active work before restarting it.
  • After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching component's installation and startup contract pass without discarding its saved state.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
